column1: # population_aliases.tsv -- labels that name the SAME or near-equivalent ancestry
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Sub-population gap detection compares the population
# labels on the reference side against those on the donor side. Those labels
# come from different sources with different naming conventions, so the same
# people appear under two names: 1000 Genomes YRI and HGDP Yoruba are the same
# population sampled twice. Comparing raw strings reports Yoruba as uncovered
# while YRI sits in the reference, and --ref-min-per-pop then pulls HGDP Yoruba
# samples out of the donor pool to fill a gap that does not exist -- spending
# the only donor-eligible material there is on nothing.
# COLUMNS
#   label       the population string as it appears in the panel's `pop` column
#   group       the ancestry group it belongs to; labels sharing a group are
#               treated as covering each other
#   confidence  same      the same population sampled by two projects
#               close     distinct sampling, same regional ancestry, expected
#                         to be interchangeable for a reference panel
#   source      which dataset uses this label
# ONLY `same` IS APPLIED BY DEFAULT. `close` rows are read but not used unless
# --alias-confidence close is passed, because "near enough for a reference
# panel" is a judgement about the analysis, not a fact about the data, and it
# should be made deliberately. Edit this file rather than the code.
# WHICH ROWS ACTUALLY DO ANYTHING. Only 1KG samples are reference-first and
# only non-1KG samples are donor-eligible, so a row changes behaviour only if
# it puts a non-1KG label in the same group as a 1KG label. A group whose
# members are all 1KG, or all non-1KG, is documentation rather than logic, and
# so is a singleton row: it records "checked, nothing covers this".
# LABEL SPELLING IS LOAD-BEARING. The panel carries the gnomAD/Koenig HGDP
# spellings -- BiakaPygmy, MbutiPygmy, Italian, Mongola, Melanesian, Papuan,
# and a single merged Han -- NOT the Bergstrom 2020 / Sanger WGS spellings
# (Biaka, Mbuti, BergamoItalian, Mongolian, Bougainville, PapuanHighlands +
# PapuanSepik, Han + NorthernHan). Rows for both spellings are below so that a
# relabel cannot silently re-open every gap. Re-check after any relabel with:
#   awk -F'\t' '!/^#/ && NR>1 {print $1}' reference_ids/population_aliases.tsv \
#     | sort -u > /tmp/a
#   awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 {print $3}' reference_ids/lai_ref_panel_samples.tsv \
#     | sort -u > /tmp/p
#   comm -23 /tmp/a /tmp/p    # labels in this file that no sample carries
# LABELS BELOW THAT NO SAMPLE CARRIES YET. These are inert until the source is
# merged; they are here so the merge does not need a second audit. SGDP:
# Luhya, Esan, Mende, Gambian, BantuHerero, BantuTswana, Ju_hoan_North,
# Spanish, Finnish, English, Bergamo, Kinh, Punjabi, Bengali, Mayan, Piapoco,
# Zapotec, BedouinB, Saharawi. Bergstrom/Sanger HGDP relabel: Biaka, Mbuti,
# BergamoItalian, NorthernHan, Mongolian, Bougainville, PapuanHighlands and
# PapuanSepik. Almarri: none written, see the MEN block.
# SGDP IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE FOR MOST POPULATIONS. 132 of the 277 rows
# in reference_ids/sgdp_manifest.tsv carry an HGDP individual ID in `alias`,
# and about 20 more carry a 1KG individual ID: SGDP Luhya is NA19023/NA19044
# (1KG LWK), SGDP Mende is HG03078/HG03085 (1KG MSL), SGDP Spanish is
# HG01503/HG01504 (1KG IBS), SGDP English is HG00126/HG00128 (1KG GBR), SGDP
# Ju_hoan_North is four HGDP San individuals, SGDP Papuan is fifteen HGDP
# Papuan individuals. For those the right action is duplicate removal
# (known_duplicate_pairs.tsv, 1e_king_dedup), not an alias row. The rows below
# only stop the gap check reporting them as uncovered ancestries meanwhile.
# DELIBERATELY NOT ALIASED. Some labels look similar and are not:
#   Basque, Sardinian, Kalash, San, MbutiPygmy, BiakaPygmy  -- genetic isolates
#       or deeply divergent lineages with no 1000 Genomes counterpart. Treating
#       any of them as covered by a neighbour defeats the purpose of the gap
#       check. Note the panel spellings: MbutiPygmy, BiakaPygmy.
#   SGDP Khomani_San -- a different San group from HGDP San (Ju|'hoansi,
#       Namibia), and admixed. Not grouped with San.
#   Italian (HGDP, Bergamo, Lombardy, 46N 10E) vs TSI/Tuscan (43N 11E) -- both
#       Italian, opposite ends of the peninsula's north-centre gradient.
#   Russian, Adygei, BantuSouthAfrica, Melanesian, Papuan and every MEN label
#       -- real, unfilled reference gaps. No 1KG population covers them at any
#       confidence, so samples spent there are genuinely spent.
#   MXB Nahua, Totonac, Tzotzil, Huichol, Tarahumara, Zapotec/Mazatec, and
#       SGDP Mixe, Quechua, Chane, Masai, Luo, Dinka -- no 1KG counterpart.
#   CEU   -- Utah residents of northern/western European ancestry. Broad and
#       not equivalent to any single HGDP population. Usable only as a `close`
#       cover for NW European labels; see the nwest_europe group.
#   ACB, ASW -- 1000 Genomes African-ancestry populations in the Americas are
#       ADMIXED. Not a substitute for any continental African population.
#   PEL, MXL, CLM, PUR -- 1000 Genomes American populations are ADMIXED, not
#       Indigenous American, and are not a substitute for MXB or HGDP
#       Indigenous populations. In the supervised run in
#       lai_ref_panel_samples.tsv (K=5) mean Q_AMR is PEL 0.723, MXL 0.438,
#       CLM 0.227, PUR 0.111. At HOMOG_THRESHOLD=0.93, CLM, PUR and MXL
#       contribute nothing, but PEL contributes 9 of 85 (5 of 85 at 0.95) and
#       those 9 already carry included=1. So "mostly will not clear the bar" is
#       right, and the 9 that do clear it are not noise: that is more AMR
#       reference samples than any single HGDP Indigenous population gives
#       (Karitiana 7, Maya 7, Pima 6, Colombian 5, Surui 4), and being 1KG they
#       cost no donor material. Keep them. Do NOT alias PEL to an Indigenous
#       label to justify them -- that would declare Quechua, Nahua and Maya
#       "covered", which is false.
#   Hazara, Uygur (EAS + West Eurasian), Makrani, Mozabite (Sub-Saharan
#       component) -- admixed by construction and will fail a Q>=0.93
#       single-component bar whatever the aliasing says.
label
YRI
Yoruba
# HGDP has NO Luhya. The Kenyan HGDP label is BantuKenya, sampled at 3S 37E in
# central/eastern Kenya, while LWK is Luhya from Webuye at ~0.6N 34.8E in
# western Kenya: both Bantu-speaking Kenyans, different ethnic groups -> close.
# SGDP's Luhya pair are 1KG LWK individuals.
LWK
Luhya
BantuKenya
ESN
Esan
# HGDP has NO Mende. MSL's only non-1KG namesake is SGDP's, and those two
# samples are 1KG MSL individuals (HG03078, HG03085).
MSL
Mende
# GWD is Mandinka: the 1KG population is recorded as "Gambian in Western
# Division - Mandinka" (NCBI BioSample). HGDP Mandenka are Mandinka at 12N 12W
# in eastern Senegal, ~400 km from the Gambian collection. Same population
# sampled by two projects -> same, not close.
GWD
Mandenka
Gambian
# Southern-African Bantu: a real gap, no 1KG cover at any confidence. These
# rows only bridge label systems -- SGDP BantuHerero and BantuTswana are HGDP
# BantuSouthAfrica individuals (HGDP01028/01035 and HGDP01030/01034).
BantuSouthAfrica
BantuHerero
BantuTswana
# Cross-spelling rows for the African isolates. Not aliases to anything in
# 1KG; they only stop one isolate being counted twice under two spellings.
BiakaPygmy
Biaka
MbutiPygmy
Mbuti
San
Ju_hoan_North
TSI
Tuscan
# HGDP has NO Spanish. The Spanish label is SGDP's, and those two samples are
# 1KG IBS individuals (HG01503, HG01504) -- stronger than "close": same people.
IBS
Spanish
FIN
Finnish
# NW Europe. GBR, CEU and SGDP English (= 1KG GBR individuals) are 1KG and are
# never spent; French and Orcadian are HGDP and are. Whether CEU/GBR cover
# them is a judgement -> close, off by default. Delete the French and Orcadian
# rows if you would rather keep them as declared gaps.
GBR
English
CEU
French
Orcadian
# HGDP Italian is the Bergamo (Lombardy) sample. Deliberately NOT grouped with
# TSI/Tuscan. SGDP Bergamo are HGDP Italian individuals (HGDP01153, HGDP01172).
Italian
BergamoItalian
Bergamo
Russian
Adygei
# One `han` group deliberately ignores the Han north-south cline, which is the
# dominant axis of Han structure: CHB is Beijing (39.9N), CHS is Hunan/Fujian
# (~26N), and the panel's single HGDP `Han` label merges Bergstrom's Han
# (32.3N 114E, central China, n=33) with NorthernHan (34.7N 107.8E, n=10).
# CHB and CHS are NOT the same population as each other. This group asserts
# only that 1KG Han cover HGDP Han well enough for a reference panel. If
# sub-Han resolution ever matters, replace the four rows with:
#   CHB  han_north  same  1KG   /  NorthernHan  han_north  same  HGDP
#   CHS  han_south  same  1KG   /  Han          han_south  same  HGDP
CHB
CHS
Han
NorthernHan
JPT
Japanese
# CDX is "Chinese Dai in Xishuangbanna"; HGDP Dai are at 21N 100E, which is
# Xishuangbanna. Same population.
CDX
Dai
# KHV (Kinh, Ho Chi Minh City) is the only mainland-SEA 1KG population. SGDP
# Kinh are 1KG KHV individuals. HGDP Cambodian (Khmer, 12N 105E) is ~700 km
# away and a different ethnic group -> close.
KHV
Kinh
Cambodian
# Cross-spelling rows only; none of these has a 1KG counterpart.
Mongola
Mongolian
Miao
Yi
GIH
# PJL is Punjabi from Lahore (31.5N 74.3E). HGDP has no Punjabi; SGDP does, and
# its four samples are 1KG PJL individuals. HGDP Sindhi (25.5N 69E) is a
# different Indo-Aryan group ~850 km south -> close, not same.
PJL
Punjabi
Sindhi
BEB
Bengali
# STU is Sri Lankan Tamil sampled in the UK and ITU Indian Telugu sampled in
# the UK -- diaspora collections. Do not alias either to SGDP's South Indian
# caste-structured groups (Irula, Mala, Madiga, Relli, Kapu, Yadava, Brahmin).
STU
ITU
# HGDP gives Balochi and Brahui the SAME coordinates (30.5N 66.5E). Brahui are
# Dravidian-speaking and Balochi Indo-Iranian, and the published reading is
# that geography predicts their genetic relationship better than language does
# (Pagani et al., Man in India 2016, on the HGDP-CEPH Brahui and Balochi).
Balochi
Brahui
Makrani
Pathan
Burusho
Hazara
# WARNING: HGDP and MXB BOTH use the bare string `Maya` in the panel's `pop`
# column, so they are already pooled by string identity and no alias row can
# separate them. They are the same population in ancestry terms -- HGDP Maya at
# 19N 91W (Campeche) and MXB Maya from Yucatan, Quintana Roo, Campeche and
# Tabasco -- but not in admixture: Q_AMR is mean 0.868 / min 0.626 across the
# 21 HGDP Maya (7 pass 0.93) against 1.000 for all 7 MXB Maya. That gap is the
# homogeneity filter's job, not an alias row's. If you disambiguate the panel's
# `pop` strings, replace the Maya row with:
#   Maya_HGDP  maya  same  HGDP   /   Maya_MXB  maya  same  MXB
Maya
Mayan
# HGDP Pima are Pima Bajo in Mexico (29N 108W, Chihuahua/Sonora), NOT the
# Akimel O'odham of Arizona.
Pima
# HGDP `Colombian` is the Piapoco/Curripaco sample at 3N 68W in eastern
# Colombia -- confirmed by SGDP Piapoco being HGDP00702/HGDP00706. It has
# nothing to do with 1KG CLM (Colombians from Medellin, admixed and urban).
Colombian
Piapoco
Karitiana
Surui
# MXB `Zapotec/Mazatec` is a MERGED two-population cluster, and the slash is a
# parsing hazard worth renaming. SGDP Zapotec (Oaxaca) covers only the Zapotec
# half, so this is close, not same.
Zapotec/Mazatec
Zapotec
# No 1000 Genomes counterpart exists for any of these, so every sample spent
# here is genuinely spent. The SGDP rows are HGDP individuals re-sequenced.
Bedouin
BedouinB
Druze
Palestinian
Mozabite

# ALMARRI 2021 -- enumerated from ~/almarri_vcfs/meta/appg.meta. Sample IDs
# are <COUNTRY><number>; the population label is the country. Counts in the
# source: UAE 57, SAUDI 29, YEMEN 21, IRAQ 13, SYRIA 12, JORDAN 3, OMAN 3.
# NONE has a 1000 Genomes counterpart, so every one is a declared gap and
# every sample spent on MEN reference is genuinely spent. These rows are
# singletons on purpose: they record "checked, nothing covers this".
# 4a cannot resolve these samples from metadata -- make_sample_groups.sh reads
# only the gnomAD HGDP+1KG file and the MXB pop file, and the SGDP manifest
# does not list them -- so without reference_ids/almarri_manifest.tsv (or 4a's
# ID-pattern fallback) all 137 resolve to super_pop=NA and are hard-excluded.
# Build the manifest with scripts/build-almarri-manifest.sh.
IRAQ
JORDAN
OMAN
SAUDI
SYRIA
UAE
YEMEN
# OPTIONAL Arabian-Peninsula grouping, OFF by default. SAUDI, UAE, OMAN and
# YEMEN are geographically and genetically adjacent, and treating them as one
# group would make --ref-min-per-pop pull 3 for the set rather than 3 each.
# Left off because Almarri 2021 reports real structure among them and MEN
# donors are not the scarce ones (SAS is). To enable, change these four to a
# shared group and run with --alias-confidence close:
#   SAUDI  arabia  close  Almarri   /   UAE    arabia  close  Almarri
#   OMAN   arabia  close  Almarri   /   YEMEN  arabia  close  Almarri
# SGDP Jordanian (Jordan214, Jordan445, Jordan603) is NOT aliased to Almarri
# JORDAN: whether they overlap at the individual level is a KING question, not
# a naming one, and 1e will answer it.
# No 1000 Genomes Oceanian population exists. These rows only bridge label
# systems; they never save a donor.
Melanesian
Bougainville
Papuan
PapuanHighlands
PapuanSepik
